entities.summary: John Catlin was an American lawyer, politician, railroad executive, and Wisconsin pioneer. He was the last secretary of the Wisconsin Territory and briefly served as acting governor of the territory after the creation of the state of Wisconsin but before the Minnesota Territory was formally organized from the remnant, between June 23, 1848, and March 3, 1849. He was also a founding member of the Wisconsin Historical Society. Earlier in his career, he was the first district attorney for Dane County, Wisconsin, and served in the legislature of the Wisconsin Territory during the 4th Wisconsin Territorial Assembly.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As the last secretary of the Wisconsin Territory and acting governor from June 23, 1848, to March 3, 1849, John Catlin played a crucial role in shaping the state's early governance. His leadership during this period had significant regional impact on the development of the American Midwest.
